subject: Sustained autoscaler queue backpressure — customer remediation check-in
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@lumenai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Sustained autoscaler queue backpressure — immediate mitigations and next steps

Samir —

I want to apologize up front for the interruption this morning to your Dedicated pool in us-west-2. We observed a sustained queue buildup impacting LumenAI’s reserved GPU pool starting ~08:45 PST; that manifested as elevated tail latency and intermittent throttling for some of your inference routes.

What happened (brief):
- Autoscaler evaluation missed a transient warmup probe regression on a subset of warm standby nodes. The result was fewer nodes reported as "Ready" during the critical scaling window, so the allocator did not trigger scale-up quickly enough.
- At the same time, KV cache thrash on the older model variant increased per-request startup cost which amplified queue growth.

Immediate mitigations we applied (already in progress):
1) Manually added 4 warm nodes to your pool to increase capacity and lower queuing.
2) Temporarily routed ~20% of traffic to a compatible lower-memory model variant (same family) to reduce KV pressure.
3) Increased the autoscaler sampling window and applied a short-term override to the min_capacity to avoid rapid oscillation while we root-cause.

Attachments: redwood-runbook-dedicated-queue.pdf (short checklist), timeline-20270427.csv (events/log markers), kvcache-log-snippet.txt (excerpt).

Next steps we are executing now:
- Infra is investigating the warmup probe regression and potential correlation with runtime v1.9.2 kernel handshake timeouts.
- We will run a targeted repro on a staging cluster to validate the fix and then push a runtime patch if necessary.
- I’ll provide an ETA for full recovery and a timeline for the postmortem within 3 business days.

Please let me know if you want us to trigger a cross-region failover to your eu-west-1 fallback while we finish the remediation (this will involve short reconfiguration on your side to point evaluation traffic).

Again, sincerely sorry for the impact. We’ll stay on this until you’re back to normal.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sustained autoscaler queue backpressure — LumenAI impact and asks

Quick technical summary and proposed fix plan:
- Root cause (preliminary): a regression in the runtime’s probe-handshake path when combined with certain driver versions produced spiky probe latencies (~800-1,200ms) for warm standby containers. The controller interprets that as nodes not Ready within the sampling window, suppressing scale-up.
- Why it amplified: Lumen’s route uses a higher-concurrency batch size and the older model variant has a heavier KV warm path, so startup IO caused a cumulative delay.

Fix plan (short):
1) Patch the probe handshake to add backpressure-resilient retries (v1.9.3 - targeted canary at 14:00 PST).
2) Implement a conservative autoscaler fallback to prefer manual min_capacity if consecutive probe failures exceed threshold (hotfix applied to controller config, rolled immediately to Lumen’s pool).
3) Run a controlled replay of the traffic spike in staging with the patched runtime to validate the end-to-end behavior.

Customer-facing steps we recommend to avoid recurrence:
- Reduce per-request concurrency on your high-throughput routes by 10-15% for the next 48 hours.
- Switch to the lower-memory model variant as we did for the transient window (we will keep that routing for 2 hours then revert).

I’ll produce a short note for Support and the CS team to send to Lumen with the timeline.csv and kvcache-log-snippet.txt attached.

—Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Update: LumenAI dedicated pool — remediation applied and credit proposal

Samir —

Update and summary:
- Manual scale executed at 08:55 PST: added 4 warm nodes; queue drained by ~09:05 PST and tail latencies returned to baseline by 09:20 PST.
- Hotfix: infra deployed autoscaler/controller config hotfix to prefer min_capacity on sustained probe anomalies at 14:00 PST. Patch to runtime probe-handshake (v1.9.3) is in canary and will go to staged rollout pending verification.
- Recommended customer actions: reduce concurrency by 10% for 48h (we can automate a rollout if you want), keep the temporary lower-memory variant routing for 2 hours (we will revert unless you ask otherwise).

Credit proposal: Karthik proposed a 10% usage credit applied to LumenAI’s monthly reserved bill for the impacted period; he’ll follow up with exact numbers and a formal doc in the next 24 hours.

Attached: redwood-runbook-dedicated-queue.pdf and timeline-20270427.csv. Full postmortem will be delivered within 3 business days and will include root cause, actions taken, mitigation timeline, and code changes (if applicable).

If you’re comfortable with the credit proposal, we’ll start the paperwork and send a short customer-facing note for your internal teams. Appreciate your patience and again sorry for the disruption.

—
